name: Darbang
blurb: A market village on the Myagdi Khola, one and a half to two hours by jeep west of Beni, where the road section of the Dhaulagiri approach has traditionally ended. It is the last place with well-stocked shops before the trek.

name: Dharapani
blurb: A ridge-top village above the Myagdi Khola that gives the first clear look at Dhaulagiri and Gurja Himal. Not the Dharapani on the Annapurna Circuit; this one is a few hours' walk above Darbang.

name: Muri
blurb: A large Magar village on a terrace high above the Myagdi Khola and the last settlement of any size on the route. Beyond it the trail leaves farmland for steep grass slopes and forest.

name: Boghara
blurb: The last permanent village, a few terraced farms on a steep hillside above the Myagdi Khola. The path to it crosses exposed grass slopes and rock steps. From here to Marpha there are only seasonal huts and campsites.

name: Dobang
blurb: A forest clearing beside the Myagdi Khola with a seasonal tea shop and room for tents. The day from Boghara is all up and down through dense, damp forest, with side streams crossed on log bridges.

name: Sallaghari
blurb: A campsite among pines where the forest begins to thin and the west wall of Dhaulagiri closes in overhead. Crews use slightly different sites along this stretch, so the height you are quoted may be anywhere from 2,800 to 3,100 m.

name: Italian Base Camp
blurb: A grassy shelf under the west face of Dhaulagiri I and the last comfortable campsite before the glacier. Parties normally spend two nights here to acclimatize, and it is the usual point for a helicopter pick-up if someone has to go out.
tip: Cross the rockfall zone above camp early, before the sun reaches the slopes, and wear a helmet if your crew carries them.

name: Glacier Camp
blurb: A cramped campsite on the rubble-covered Chhonbardan Glacier, in the gorge between Dhaulagiri I and Tsaurabong Peak. Tent platforms are levelled on ice and stones, and rockfall from both walls can be heard through the night.

name: Dhaulagiri Base Camp
blurb: The expedition base on the upper Chhonbardan Glacier, directly beneath the north face of Dhaulagiri I, with Tukuche Peak and the icefall to the north-east col across the ice. The second acclimatization stop before the passes.
tip: Sleep here two nights. If anyone is unwell, go back down the glacier; do not carry on over French Pass hoping it will improve.

name: French Pass
blurb: The 5,360 m saddle between the Chhonbardan Glacier and Hidden Valley and the highest point of the circuit. It is named after the 1950 French expedition, which reconnoitred Dhaulagiri here before turning to Annapurna.

name: Hidden Valley
blurb: A wide, bare valley at about 5,000 m between French Pass and Dhampus Pass, where every group camps at least one night. It is the coldest and highest camp of the trek, and both ways out cross a pass above 5,200 m. Quoted heights run from 5,000 to 5,200 m.
tip: Expect minus 15 to minus 20 °C at night in season. Keep water bottles in your sleeping bag and boots inside the tent.

name: Dhampus Pass
blurb: The exit from Hidden Valley towards the Kali Gandaki, between Tukuche Peak and Dhampus Peak. The climb to it is short, but the far side is a long traverse above 5,000 m across slopes that avalanche after fresh snow.

name: Yak Kharka
blurb: A herders' pasture on the hillside above Marpha and the first camp below the snowline after Dhampus Pass. Reaching it means more than 1,500 m of descent from the pass. Not the Yak Kharka on the Annapurna Circuit.

name: Dhampus Peak
blurb: A 6,012 m summit above Dhampus Pass, sometimes added to the circuit from a high camp near the pass. It is a snow climb that needs a separate climbing permit, crampons, axe and rope, and at least one extra day.
